sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. City Pulse is a cinema-to-platform acquisition special situation rather than an evidence-backed compounder. Its legacy revenue recovered to ₹5.02 crore and reported FY26 PAT reached ₹2.28 crore, but purchased goodwill, physical-cash concentration, unreliable cash-flow detail and newly acquired payment-service economics prevent a supported whole-group return estimate. The new Sunshine agreement is a real commercial opportunity, not verified cash or recurring earnings. At the secondary 19 October close of ₹106.95, the funded legacy/advertising boundary is insufficient on its own; new target value could change that conclusion, but cannot be fabricated. Clarified group accounts, target net-fee profitability/settlement liabilities and cash collection are the decisive next evidence. [S2][S6][S7][S8]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Cutoff: 20 October 2026, UTC. City Pulse Multiventures Limited, formerly City Pulse Multiplex, BSE 542727/CPML, ISIN INE056001014. Original prospectus and BSE-SME identity are verified; the interop date field is not used as its original IPO date. The official master and October listing notice reconcile 14,938,833 current shares, giving ₹159.77 crore at ₹106.95. Lot 50 costs ₹5,347.50 at that dated price. The reference position is ₹5 lakh, not a recommendation. AS financial statements, not an assumed Ind AS template, are used. Reported group scope is primary, with constant-parent operating history shown separately and new targets excluded from fabricated profits. Five investor years end 19 October 2031; the annual model includes the March-to-October terminal stub. Equity hurdle is an analytical 15%, with 12%/18% sensitivity; it is not WACC. Identity confidence is High, parent P&L and historical growth Medium, but group cash/target economics Low. G1 Conditional, G2 Hold, G3 Conditional and G4 Conditional, with precise effects in the gate register. [S2][S4][S7][S13][MX1][MX2]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Supported factors: GOV 4, MOAT 3, REV 4, DUR 5, CAP 3, EXEC 4 and EARN 4. CASH and BAL are NS for material cash/perimeter gaps, not neutral scores. R/D/P remain NS because newly acquired target profits and obligations are not reliably modeled; L is a conditional 1 for the stated ₹5 lakh position. Exact weights, contributions, coverage and mathematical missing-data bounds are shown in the audit. BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS and are not rankable. The capital-return weakness applies the framework GQS ceiling of 5 only if a full raw score becomes computable; it never replaces NS. No integrity failure is asserted and no blanket governance override is applied. The REV window exception is explicitly documented in Section 6 rather than choosing a pandemic-base growth rate. [E1–E13]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The original business earns cinema exhibition, food/product sales, advertising and rent-related income. Customers choose a cinema on location, film availability, format and price; cash realization depends on ticket/platform settlement and commercial counterparties. July 2025 transaction materials described 13 Gujarat screens, but a current audited screen-level revenue/occupancy bridge is not available. The company is expanding into WOWPLEX digital content, Matrubharti regional-language literature and ERECH payment services. Those are different businesses: a content platform must convert audience/IP into retained subscription or advertising income, while a payment operator may process large flows but retain only a small fee. The ERECH filing labels FY26 turnover ₹4,035.59 crore; without principal-agent and settlement accounting, it is not added to legacy cinema revenue or valued at a cinema margin. Sunshine compensation is based on qualifying views and campaign rates. The ₹9 crore billing/payment term is neither proof of receipt nor a second revenue stream on top of the same views. [S2][S6][S8][S9][S10]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Location and customer familiarity can help an individual cinema, but no exclusive catchment, sustained pricing premium or market-share denominator has been demonstrated. Regional authors/readers could create network benefits through content variety and engagement; active paying cohorts, retention, acquisition cost and rights ownership are needed to establish that mechanism. A registered valuation or audience claim is not itself moat evidence. Three primary comparators show the competitive challenge: Connplex reported 113 screens and ₹147.52 crore FY26 revenue, including ₹64.81 crore cinema-making/franchise fees; Cineline reported 85 screens, ₹242.05 crore pre-Ind AS revenue and 14.7% EBITDA margin; PVR INOX disclosed 1,802 screens on 23 March. These establish distribution/format competition, not transferable valuation multiples. City Pulse’s reported 76.5% FY26 EBITDA margin is not accepted as proof of superior cinema unit economics without segment and rent reconciliation. A capable entrant can obtain conventional projection/F&B capability; proprietary content monetization and sustained audience switching costs remain unproven. [P1][P2][P3][S2][S10]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Historical parent operating revenue was ₹3.0896 crore in the FY19 prospectus, ₹3.2425 crore in FY20, ₹0.0511 crore in FY21, ₹0.4717 crore in FY22, ₹0.4832 crore in the later FY23 comparative, then ₹1.1490/2.8131/5.0227 crore in FY24–26. FY23 originally labeled ₹0.5510 crore as revenue; FY24 separates ₹0.0677 crore other income, with essentially unchanged total income/PAT. This is a disclosed two-sided reclassification, not an unexplained missing sale. Annual operating additions in FY24–26 are ₹0.6658/1.6641/2.2096 crore. The optical three-year FY23–26 CAGR is 118.24% and five-year FY21–26 CAGR 150.32%, but both start from severely depressed cinema recovery bases. The explicit scoring exception uses the six-year FY20–26 full-cycle CAGR of 7.566%, mapping to REV 4 under the unchanged numerical rubric; FY19–26 provides a similar roughly 7% cross-check. A ten-year CAGR lacks the required eleven comparable observations. June 2026 revenue fell 1.53%; group PAT fell 38.46%. The diagnostic TTM revenue is ₹5.0053 crore, using FY26 plus current June minus prior June, not annualizing one quarter. New acquired turnover is shown separately; volume/price and organic unit decomposition remain ND. [S2][S3][S7][S11–S15]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The accessible avenues are existing cinema utilization, proposed Khokhra screens, regional content monetization and the signed advertising relationship. Solar/GIFT City/education themes on the website do not enter the model without project economics and funding. The ₹85.26 crore Aileensoul share consideration must remain in capital employed, even though it was not cash capex. The financial-capital proxy gives roughly 2.5% FY26 NOPAT return including goodwill; excluding ₹85.68 crore goodwill would spuriously suggest very strong returns. A FY23–26 incremental proxy uses loss-period operating EBIT after excluding other income, no assumed tax credit, and the change in equity plus debt less reported cash: approximately ₹3.10 crore incremental NOPAT over ₹85.25 crore capital, or 3.6%, not a project IRR. This is below the analytical 12–18% cost-of-capital range and remains subject to scope/cash caveats. The model explicitly funds capex, WC, the ₹4.0013 crore ERECH acquisition and continuing target support; it does not derive growth from a headline TAM. Sunshine renewals and purchased-target value are separate assumptions. GQS remains NS because normalized cash realization is unresolved, with the CAP-related ceiling shown separately. [S2][S6][S8][S14]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The promoter family occupies executive and finance roles. FY26 note-level promoter percentages total about 11.98% before the subsequent swap; a current post-allotment beneficial-ownership and encumbrance reconciliation is still needed, so this is not asserted as current free float or an unpledged-holding certification. The original IPO sought ₹3.984 crore gross, ₹3.46 crore net, including ₹2.7059 crore for new miniplex/multiplex facilities and ₹0.7541 crore general purposes. Complete object-wise use and unit commissioning outcomes are not independently reconstructed from the original prospectus alone. On 29 February 2024, 7.35 million shares at ₹116 funded Aileensoul’s ₹85.26 crore acquisition without cash proceeds. Matrubharti’s initial 2025 proposal was ₹153.0772 crore in shares; approval/listing was delayed and FY26 note 21 excluded it historically. October listing of 4,274,800 shares resolves current capital, but not all target accounting. The subsequent ₹4.0013 crore ERECH cash purchase and Sunshine agreement are concrete milestones; disclosed turnover is not proof of integrated profit delivery. [S2][S4][S8–S10][S13][S14]

The statutory opinion is unmodified. Nevertheless, CARO says the internal-audit report was not provided and the auditor could not opine on that system; the secretarial report identifies a delayed integrated-governance filing. CARO also lists ₹0.6118 crore undisputed income-tax/TDS arrears beyond six months. These are attributed compliance/control facts, not findings of diversion or criminal conduct. The September corrigendum merely corrects the corporate-information auditor name. Related-party note 20 labels ₹1.4893 crore as remuneration payable, while the borrowing-note director aggregate is ₹1.5284 crore; adding the ₹0.0391 crore other director balance reconciles the aggregate, so these are not charged twice as separate model claims. Classification, interest and settlement terms still deserve clarification. No unsupported assurance about all litigation, pledges or connected counterparties is given. [S2][S5]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The historical table preserves reported P&L and CFO rather than manufacturing normalized earnings. FY24–26 reported PAT was ₹0.1476/1.3444/2.2848 crore; EBITDA proxies were ₹0.4446/1.8687/3.8425 crore. Reported CFO was ₹0.3888/4.5380/2.1454 crore and cash capex ₹0.2537/2.4018/0.2949 crore, giving reported FCF proxies ₹0.1351/2.1362/1.8505 crore. The three-year ratio of sums is 1.87× CFO/PAT, but it is not an owner-cash-quality conclusion: FY25 CFO contains ₹2.3629 crore supplier-credit inflow, cash tax is not clearly settled and detailed movements do not fully reconcile. FY26 cash-flow amounts use lakh-scale values despite a rupee heading. Small closing-cash differences are not portrayed as major economic losses. [S2][S3][S14]

Original-layout verification shows the FY26 comparative asset imbalance largely results from omitting the prior ₹85.6825 crore intangible/goodwill line; the FY25 original contains it. Current FY26 totals balance. Separate group-audit wording describes nil subsidiary amounts and contradictory reliance on an unfurnished report; that scope issue is unresolved. Reported cash is ₹6.8356 crore, of which ₹6.7460 crore is physical cash and only ₹0.0896 crore bank balance. This is a verification priority, not proof cash is missing. Receivables include ₹0.8538 crore classified doubtful out of ₹1.2194 crore. Collection haircuts reduce opening collectible WC; the model does not also charge a cash write-off. Gross debt is ₹4.3344 crore despite zero reported finance cost, so forecast rates are explicit assumptions rather than extrapolated zero cost. [S2][S3]

Opening gross ONWC is ₹1.21935 crore receivables plus ₹0.15 crore advances less trade payables, operating current liabilities and ₹0.02459 crore audit expense provision. Statutory/employee/expense dues already inside that stock are not paid a second time. Net current income tax ₹0.8026728 crore is paid once after offsetting ₹0.0321709 crore TDS; shareholder money ₹0.014074 crore is refunded separately. Deferred tax ₹0.1447503 crore remains a nominal terminal claim, not an invented immediate bill. Old tax arrears may overlap recorded tax/statutory balances and are not added indiscriminately. Nonoperating advances, security-deposit assets and preliminary expenses are not treated as spare terminal cash. Reported ROE is roughly 2.47%; full-capital return diagnostics include goodwill and are not inflated by removing it. [S2]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The dated mixed-period cross-check is approximately 69.9× FY26 reported earnings on current shares and 40.9× legacy EBITDA after reported March debt/cash; neither is a verified post-acquisition group multiple. The main valuation is a linked legacy/advertising operating model plus separately bounded target-stake equity. Bear/base/bull legacy growth paths, margins of 25%/40%/50%, WC ratios of 20%/12%/8%, capex, tax, acquisitions and cash support are explicit in the model. Base assumes ₹9 crore Sunshine revenue and collection only in FY27, with a 35% contribution margin; bull assumes renewal, bear none. These are analyst conditions, not achieved contracts or earnings. New borrowing carries half-year interest, tax/draw circularity is solved, and ordinary repayments occur at year-end. No unapproved facility or equity rescue is claimed. [S2][S6][S8]

With additional target-stake equity set to zero as a boundary, five-year terminal prices are ₹0.00/₹18.89/₹81.01, corresponding to -100.00%/-29.30%/-5.40% annualized returns. Peak debt including opening debt is ₹18.22/₹4.33/₹4.33 crore. Zero added target value is not a conclusion that the targets are worthless. Adding ₹25/75/153.08 crore of net, non-overlapping terminal target equity to the base gives approximately −19.74%/−8.37%/+2.56% annualized returns. The base legacy path needs another ₹293.14 crore terminal target equity to reach the 15% hurdle, versus ₹253.35/337.30 crore at 12%/18%. Actual target profits, take rates, debt and reinvestment must support that value. The 3×3 margin/multiple table and cash-on-hand/advertising sensitivities are fully linked, not isolated EPS proxies. The legacy-only 15% hurdle entry of ₹9.39 is not a whole-company fair-value target. [E11][MX2]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest positive counterargument is that the purchased platforms and Sunshine monetization create substantial value not captured by legacy cinema results. The strongest bear case is the opposite: monetization disappoints, receivables collect poorly, physical cash is not fully deployable, project spending continues and payment-settlement obligations emerge. The linked severe case uses bank cash only, no advertising revenue, weak margins, slow WC and target cash support; it requires peak debt of ₹42.47 crore and leaves modeled common equity at zero before any independently proven target recovery. This is a funding requirement, not a forecast of certain bankruptcy or evidence of misconduct. Impairment risk is High because purchased value and cash availability dominate shareholder recovery; the single decisive variable is sustainable, distributable net earnings from the acquired platforms after their own obligations. A lower share price cannot by itself resolve an unknown liability perimeter. [S2][S6][S8][E11]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Over five years, 5×/10× price outcomes require terminal common equity of ₹798.85/₹1597.71 crore at unchanged 14,938,833 shares, before any new dilution. The funded legacy base is only about ₹28.22 crore terminal equity. Most of either outcome would therefore have to come from newly monetized platforms, not simply recovering cinema utilization. Capital requirements, target debt, cash distributions and dilution must be included; the share-swap price is not proof of terminal value. A lower terminal multiple is already tested. Classification: speculative/unsupported on present operating evidence, not a precise success probability. [E5][E11]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Review the next filed results, including the meeting rescheduled for 23 October, rather than assuming outcomes after the cutoff. Track: (1) post-listing capital and target consolidation against 14,938,833 shares; any unresolved perimeter is a valuation hold, not automatic misconduct; (2) Matrubharti audited net revenue/PAT and the replacement valuation report, comparing actual monetization with the large consideration; (3) ERECH retained fee, settlement assets/liabilities and cash obligation, not turnover alone; (4) Sunshine invoices, earned revenue, receipts and cancellation/renewal terms, with uncollected FY27 billing invalidating the base cash assumption; (5) bankable cash against March physical cash ₹6.7460 crore, with independent reconciliation needed before liquidity comfort; (6) doubtful receivables ₹0.8538 crore and provision/collection outcome; (7) cash-tax/statutory arrears and opening-claim settlements, without double counting; (8) group-audit wording and internal-audit availability; (9) current lot, BSE surveillance and 60-session executable trading capacity, with live depth checked before implementation. Normal quarterly volatility is not a thesis break, but persistent failure to establish target net economics prevents an investment conclusion. [S2][S6][S8][S16][MX1][MX2]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved; acquisition special situation, not an evidence-backed compounder. Supported historical factors are retained, but BQS/GQS/IAS are incomplete and excluded from point-score rankings. The action is further evidence-led research, not a buy/sell instruction. Current target economics and liabilities, cash verification and reconciled reporting could materially improve or worsen the conclusion; merely assuming target consideration equals value cannot. Even if business evidence improves, the ₹5 lakh reference exit test remains restrictive and must be rerun with actual intended position size and live order-book conditions. An existing holder would additionally need portfolio weight, taxes and execution constraints before any reduce/exit decision. [S2][S8][MX2]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary annual reports, original-layout checks, prospectus and transaction/results disclosures underpin the historical facts; source dates and inspected locations are in the ledger. The secondary listing mirror is corroborated by official current capital, but not passed off as a directly retrieved BSE original. Secondary OHLCV is identified as a turnover proxy, with one missing calendar observation bounded rather than zero-filled. The registered replacement target valuation report is known from an August 2025 filing index but was not recovered after reviewing the issuer page and focused searches. Crucial open questions are target audited profitability and settlement obligations, valuation methodology and IP rights, post-allotment beneficial ownership/pledges, physical-cash availability, cash-flow movement reconciliation, old tax-claim overlap and project commitments. Analyst margins, cash availability, target support, entry hurdle and terminal multiples are assumptions with linked sensitivities. No reported purchase consideration, goodwill or large transaction flow is substituted for verified equity value. [S2][S4][S6][S8–S10][S18][S19][MX1][MX2]

ranking_eligibility.reason: Incomplete composites and material reliability hold; do not rank NS as a poor point score.

GOV.reason: Minority investors face weak disclosure/control discipline: the statutory auditor could not assess the internal-audit system without its report, and integrated-governance filing was late. The acquisition issue was delayed by eligibility/listing matters but subsequently listed; an unmodified audit opinion and eventual listing are contrary evidence. These facts do not prove diversion or justify G1 failure.

MOAT.reason: Operating cinemas and a signed advertising arrangement establish a real business, but neither establishes hard-to-replicate pricing or distribution power. Regional content networks could strengthen differentiation; verified retention, paid cohorts and take rates are absent, while larger exhibitors offer comparable premium formats.

REV.reason: Explicit full-cycle window exception: FY20–26 parent revenue CAGR7.566% maps to4 under the unchanged5–10% rubric. Five-year FY21 and three-year FY23 trough-based growth are shown but not scored. Current June revenue was down1.53%, only one quarter and therefore no trajectory adjustment. Acquired platform turnover is not silently added to parent organic growth.

DUR.reason: There are tangible customer/digital opportunities through Sunshine and acquired platforms, beyond an abstract TAM. Conversely the initial advertising term is one year and depends on views; target net-fee monetization and contracted renewal economics are unproven. Cinema demand also depends on content slates.

CAP.reason: The₹85.26 crore2024 share-swap commitment remained associated with₹85.68 crore goodwill throughFY26 while reported group PAT was only₹2.28 crore. Full-capital return proxy is about2.5%, below the12–18% analytical capital-cost range overFY24–26. Excluding purchased goodwill produces a misleadingly high return. Better FY26 operating profits and new commercial access are contrary evidence, but do not yet establish attractive returns on purchased capital.

CASH.reason: Reported three-year CFO/PAT is1.87×, but source cash-flow classification/units and detailed movements, cash-tax settlement and₹6.75 crore physical cash availability do not reconcile sufficiently for normalized cash realization. Doubtful receivables₹0.854 crore also require collection/provision evidence. No fabricated neutral or punitive cash score.

BAL.reason: Recorded legacy cash exceeds debt, but₹4.0013 crore acquisition consumes liquidity and the acquired payment platform settlement obligations are unavailable. Funded stresses are explicit, but a whole-group survival score would require those obligations and usable cash.

EXEC.reason: Legacy activity recovered and October listing resolved a major delayed milestone. Against that, the2024 purchased platform has not demonstrated substantial disclosed group earnings; the Matrubharti issuance took untilOctober2026 to list, and new Sunshine/ERECH milestones have not yet yielded audited integrated results. New announcements alone are not treated as delivered monetization.

EARN.reason: ReportedFY26 profits arose in the operating P&L rather than other-income gains, a positive. However EBITDA margin76.5% is not corroborated by segmented unit economics, June group PAT declined38.46%, and current-share proforma FY26EPS is₹1.529 versus reported₹2.14 before latest dilution. No invented normalized target profit.

R.reason: The conditional funded legacy model is complete, but material newly acquired targets have no reliable net-fee/PAT/settlement bridge. A zero-target-value boundary is not a defensible whole-group central forecast and therefore is not scored as R1.

D.reason: Legacy stress quantifies equity exhaustion and borrowing needs, but target assets and settlement liabilities could materially alter creditor/common-equity recovery. No point score from an incomplete group recovery perimeter.

assumption_notes: New borrowing incurs half-year interest in the year drawn. Ordinary excess-cash repayments occur at year-end and receive no same-year interest saving. Curis collateral-funded FD overdraft repayment retains its explicit half-year timing. Interest, positive-profit cash tax and funding draw are solved jointly to a 1e-12 crore tolerance; new borrowing is a funding requirement, not a committed facility.
Full FY27 bridge uses March2026 disclosed opening cash, the known subsequent ERECH cash acquisition, tax and ordinary claims. It is not a verified October balance sheet.

Reported cash on hand availability and doubtful-debt collection fractions are sensitivities, not findings of missing cash. Reducing collectible opening ONWC makes future WC funding larger; no duplicate cash write-off.

Sunshine FY27 ₹9 crore revenue and cash collection are a conditional scenario, not a verified receipt. No separate upfront cash or extra view-fee stream is added. Bull renewals are unsupported upside assumptions.

ERECH/Matrubharti target profits and acquired settlement balances are not fabricated. A separate additional stake-equity sensitivity is after target debt and minorities, net of any overlap with modeled advertising economics.

Support transfers to targets are conservatively treated as cash consumption with no second recoverable asset. Zero target-stake value is a valuation boundary, not an assertion that targets are worthless.
No assumed new equity rescue, no dividends, no swap cash proceeds. Required borrowing is not an approved facility.

Opening expense provision₹0.02459 and statutory/employee/trade dues remain in ONWC and unwind into forecast WC. Opening shareholder money₹0.014074 is refunded separately. Tax₹0.8026728 is paid once after offsetting disclosed TDS₹0.0321709.
Opening deferred tax₹0.1447503 remains a nominal terminal claim, not an immediate current cash payment. Normal forecast cash tax applies to new positive profits; no old reversal credit is assumed.

No separate addback of goodwill, Aileensoul investment, old nonoperating advances, preliminary expenses or uncertain target fair value. Lease cash operating expense is inside the margin assumptions; no capitalized lease liability is added.
Annual fiscal forecast throughFY2031 plus202-day steady-run-rate cash stub aligns the terminal date with five investor years. No additional growth or new contract is assumed in the stub.

formulas.cfo: EBITDA - interest - future positive-profit cash tax - change ONWC - one-time opening net tax
formulas.cash: opening cash + CFO - capex - acquisition - target support - shareholder refund + draw - repayment
formulas.terminal: legacy/ad EBITDA run rate × multiple + closing cash - debt - retained old deferred tax + separately assumed net target-stake equity
formulas.return_formula: (terminal common equity / current diluted shares / dated price)^(1/5) - 1
